newsitem.title: USA: Vermont Democrats win control of state senate.
newsitem.headline: Vermont Democrats win control of state senate.

text.p: Vermont Democrats won effective control of the state Senate with Doug Racine's victory in the race for lieutenant governor.
With some of the votes in state Senate races still being counted, Gov. Howard Dean said it looks like the Republicans and Democrats will have equal numbers in the chamber, with 15 members each.
The lieutenant governor breaks tie votes in the 30-member senate. Racine defeated Republican John Carroll with almost 60 percent of the votes.
Dean himself coasted to a third two-year term. The Democrat overwhelmed Republican John Gropper by more than 50 percentage points.
The governor said the Democrats will deliver on their promise of property tax reform, now that Vermont voters have ended several years of Republican control in the state senate.
Dean says the outcome guarantees that property tax reform will be enacted during the legislative session that begins in January.
